chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever complains about a need to a believer, it is as though he has complained about it to Allah; and whoever complains about it to an unbeliever, it is as though he complained about Allah.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of complaining to a believer versus an unbeliever in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the metaphysical link between the believer (al-mu'min) and Allah, portraying the believer as a manifestation of Divine attributes and a trustworthy conduit for needs. By contrasting this with the disbeliever (al-kafir), the text underscores the Shia concept of 'wilayah' and the spiritual hierarchy, where turning to a believer is an act of recognizing Divine agency in creation, while turning to a disbeliever is akin to attributing one's plight to a force disconnected from Divine mercy.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 427. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Whoever complains about a need to a believer, it is as though he has complained about it to Allāh; but whoever complains about it to an unbeliever it is as though he complained about Allāh.
